fix: improve publish workflow security, caching and new-package support (#1009)

Pin all GitHub Actions to commit SHAs, split asdf cache into
restore/save, add registry verification step, and implement
OIDC/NPM_TOKEN dual publish strategy for new packages.

fix: URL-encode scoped package names in registry verification and handle transient errors

Scoped packages (e.g. @inditextech/weave-sdk) contain a slash that
must be percent-encoded when querying the npm registry, otherwise
the check always returns 404 and falls back to NPM_TOKEN.

Also switch from if/else to case to distinguish 404 (new package)
from transient errors (429/5xx) which now fail the workflow instead
of silently falling back.

Validated in InditexTech/npm-release-testing#27.

fix: add curl timeout and retry to registry verification

Prevent the workflow from hanging indefinitely if the npm registry
is slow or unresponsive. Adds --connect-timeout 10, --max-time 30,
and --retry 3 with --retry-all-errors.

Validated in InditexTech/npm-release-testing#27.

fix: detect unpublished packages, remove redundant export PATH, scope NPM_TOKEN

- Registry verification now checks for active versions, not just
  HTTP 200. Unpublished packages (tombstones with no versions) are
  correctly treated as new, triggering NPM_TOKEN fallback.
- Remove redundant `export PATH` in asdf shims restore (GITHUB_PATH
  already handles persistence across steps).
- Scope NPM_TOKEN to a temporary npmrc via NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG
  instead of writing to the global ~/.npmrc.

Validated in InditexTech/npm-release-testing#27.

fix: handle malformed JSON in registry check, cleanup temp npmrc with trap

- Registry verification now distinguishes between "no active versions"
  (exit 1) and "JSON parse failure" (exit 2), failing the workflow on
  malformed responses instead of silently falling back to NPM_TOKEN.
- Temp npmrc is cleaned up via trap on EXIT and created with chmod 600.

Validated in InditexTech/npm-release-testing#27.

fix: fail fast when NPM_TOKEN secret is missing in new-package fallback

Add an explicit guard that checks NPM_AUTH is set before writing
the temp npmrc. Without this, a missing secret would only surface
as a generic npm auth error later in the publish step.

Validated in InditexTech/npm-release-testing#27.

fix: prevent set -e from aborting on node exit code in registry verification

Under bash -e (GitHub Actions default), a non-zero exit from the
node version-check command would abort the step before PARSE_STATUS
could be captured. Use `|| PARSE_STATUS=$?` to safely capture the
exit code without triggering set -e.

Validated in InditexTech/npm-release-testing#27.

fix: handle curl failure under set -e with explicit error message

Wrap curl in `if !` to prevent set -e from aborting the step on
curl failure. Use -sS instead of -s to show curl errors while
still suppressing progress. Emit a clear ::error:: on connectivity
failure before exiting.

Fix escaped chars on CHANGELOG.md when release process is executed (#1157)

* chore: initial commit

* fix(changelog): remove stray escapes/NBSP from CHANGELOG.md and guard against recurrence

release-flow/keep-a-changelog-action re-serializes the entire

non-breaking space (U+00A0) instead of a real ASCII space fail
CommonMark's ATX-heading rule, get parsed as plain text instead of a
heading, and the action's serializer defensively backslash-escapes
them on the way back out (`### Added` -> `\### Added`) -
corrupting content it never meant to touch, and re-corrupting it on
every future release since the underlying invisible character was
never removed.

  stray leading backslash and normalize the non-breaking space that
  caused it back to a regular space.

  line-start escapes and normalizes invisible Unicode whitespace,
  used both to sanitize and as a --check-only detector.
- Release workflow: run it right after keep-a-changelog-action in
  both the snapshot and release jobs, failing the job on purpose if
  anything needed fixing - so the defect gets fixed at its source
  (a PR) instead of being silently re-patched forever.

Fix check-links reporting issue (#1170)

* chore: initial commit

* fix(docs): don't truncate check-links output with process.exit(1)

process.exit() kills the process immediately; when stdout is a pipe
(true in CI) Node's writes to it are async, so the console.log burst
listing broken external links right before it can get truncated
before the OS drains the write queue. Seen on a real run: the log
showed "6 broken external link(s) found." but not one of the six
URLs.

Use process.exitCode instead — same non-zero exit, but the module
finishes and the event loop flushes pending stdout first.

Upstream issue filed: InditexTech/docouture#231

Use process.exitCode instead — same non-zero exit, but the module

* fix(docs): log HTTP status alongside broken external links

check-links.mjs reports which link is broken but not why. Following up
on cac07585 (docouture#231): the first live re-run after that fix
surfaced 3 URLs, only 1 of which (azure.microsoft.com/es-es/products/web-pubsub)
failed consistently across 2 separate runs — the other 2 passed clean
on run 2. That's the signature of CI-side rate limiting/timeouts, not
dead links, but there was no way to confirm without the actual status
code linkinator recorded.

link.status is 0 when the request itself never got a response
(timeout, DNS, connection reset) vs a real HTTP status when the
server did answer — logging it distinguishes "this link is actually
gone" from "this crawl's burst of concurrent requests got
rate-limited", which decides whether the fix is content (dead link)
or script (concurrency/timeout tuning).

* fix(docs): retry transient failures before reporting a link broken

Following up on cac07585 / 8e9c99e8 (docouture#231): live CI runs show
the same 3 external links flip between broken and fine run to run (3
broken, then 1, then 0) with no client anywhere else ever seeing
anything but 200 — a transient failure (rate limit, timeout, reset),
not a dead link, mis-happening to fail the whole build on a bad roll
of the dice.

linkinator already has a mechanism for exactly this that the script
wasn't using: `retry` (honour a 429's retry-after header) and
`retryErrors` (retry a 5xx or status-0/no-response result a few
times with jitter) instead of accepting the crawl's first failure as
final. Wires both up with linkinator's own documented defaults for
count/jitter.
